cases.learnNotes: A pneumothorax is air between the lung and the chest wall. Look for the visceral pleural line: a thin white line parallel to the chest wall with no lung markings beyond it. The airless lung becomes denser, and the signs of volume loss point to it: a displaced fissure, a raised hemidiaphragm, shift of the hilum or mediastinum towards the collapse and crowded ribs. cases.learnNotes: On a PA film with a good inspiration the cardiothoracic ratio is the widest transverse diameter of the heart divided by the widest inner diameter of the chest; more than 0.5 suggests an enlarged cardiac silhouette. cases.learnTitle: Lung mass on a PA chest radiograph (radiologist box)
cases.referenceSummary: One box drawn by a board-certified radiologist around the lung mass (NIH ChestX-ray14). The labels mined from this film's report are: Mass (about 90% accurate, per the dataset authors). Nothing else on the film is outlined.
cases.learnNotes: A mass is a lung opacity larger than 3 cm (smaller ones are nodules). Describe its size, margins (smooth, lobulated or spiculated), location and any cavitation, and look for what goes with it: hilar or mediastinal enlargement, an effusion, rib destruction or collapse beyond it. In an adult a lung mass must be explained; the radiograph shows it but does not give the diagnosis.

tasks.explanation: Atelectasis is loss of lung volume. The airless lung becomes denser, and the signs of volume loss point to it: a displaced fissure, a raised hemidiaphragm, shift of the hilum or mediastinum towards the collapse and crowded ribs. Thin horizontal lines at the bases are plate-like (discoid) atelectasis, usually from shallow breathing. The reference is the radiologist's box, a rectangle around the finding rather than an outline; this image has no pixel spacing, so the tolerance is counted in pixels.
